subject: Edge-seat IP allowance & ephemeral egress policy for private endpoints
messages:
From: security@halcyonhealth.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: IP allowlist + ephemeral egress design for Private Endpoint POC

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Halcyon is excited to proceed with a short POC of Redwood Private inside our VPC. Before we kick off our network team needs a concise list of requirements for: IP allowlisting (source/destination), firewall policies, egress provenance (ephemeral NAT behavior), and recommended port/FQDN allow rules so we can raise the ticket with infra.

Specifically we need:
- The set of source IPs Redwood will originate traffic from (control plane and runtime) and whether those are static or ephemeral.
- Guidance on DNS / SNI patterns we should allow (if FQDN-level allowlisting is required).
- Any mTLS or client cert requirements for outbound connections.
- Minimal port list and a short rationale for each.

We attached a template CSV for evidence mapping. Could someone on your side please fill the matrix and go over any operational caveats? We have a blackout window to schedule changes on 11/9; it would be ideal to lock requirements before then.

Best,
James Smith
Security Engineer, Halcyon Health
[attachment: halcyon_requested_evidence.csv]
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: security@halcyonhealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP allowlist + ephemeral egress design for Private Endpoint POC

James — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (network security) and Laura (deploy ops) who will own the specifics.

High level summary we can commit to immediately:
- Control plane (management) traffic: a set of static Redwoods egress IPs for the control plane. We will provide the full list and commit to a 30-day notice window for changes.
- Runtime egress from Private endpoints: supports two modes — static egress IP allocation (reserved NAT per-customer) or ephemeral egress via shared NAT pool. For the POC we recommend reserved NAT to simplify allowlisting during initial onboarding.
- FQDN-level allowlisting: supported and recommended where customers use host-based outbound controls; we will provide canonical FQDNs and SNI patterns.
- Ports: 443 (TLS) for control and runtime outbound; 853/8530 only if you plan on mTLS-based DNS or custom tunnel health checks — we can avoid these in the POC.

Kimberly — can you prepare the filled evidence matrix and include the static control-plane IPs and the reserved NAT allocation example? Laura — please add any ops caveats (route advertisement, health-check egress). I’ll join the infra call if helpful.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, security@halcyonhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP allowlist + ephemeral egress design for Private Endpoint POC

Hi James / Ben / team — attaching the completed evidence matrix and an excerpted firewall snippet you can paste into your change ticket. Notes below and caveats at the end.

Attachment: ben_egress_matrix.pdf, fw_snippets.txt

What we provided in the matrix:
- Control plane IPs (static): 3 addresses for management/control (listed in the PDF). We will provide a signed notice of any IP changes 30 days in advance. These IPs are used for deployment orchestration, model version rollouts, and telemetry ingestion.
- Reserved NAT example (recommended for POC): we can allocate one /29 for customer egress to guarantee a single deterministic outbound IP for runtime traffic. If reserved NAT is selected, traffic will appear from those addresses for all outbound TLS connections.
- Shared ephemeral NAT pool: if you want to avoid IP leasing, we can use our shared egress pool — IPs rotate; we only support short-term guarantee (minutes to hours), so allowlisting by IP is not possible in that mode.
- FQDNs / SNI: canonical SNI patterns are: *.redwood-inference.com, runtime.redwood-inference.com, model-updates.redwood-inference.com. We also recommend allowing outbound resolution to your DNS resolver to avoid split-DNS issues.
- mTLS / client certs: Not required for regular runtime outbound flows (TLS with server certs). mTLS is available for vendor integrations on a per-contract basis.
- Ports: 443 outbound (required), 22 inbound only for ops bastion access (if you opt into SSH-based troubleshooting), and 123/1230 only for time sync when using certain appliance modes (we avoid this for POC).

Operational caveats:
- If you choose reserved NAT, remember to update any per-tenant routing to avoid hairpinning through your NAT gateway.
- Egress telemetry can be toggled to provide per-token / per-request headers for debugging, but that may expose additional metadata — we can provide an opt-in mask.
- Health checks from our mesh may probe ephemeral endpoints; if you have strict allowlists, please include the control-plane static IPs.

Next steps: Laura, David — can you review the snippets for route and firewall insertion and confirm whether a /29 example suffices for the POC?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Network Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachments: ben_egress_matrix.pdf; fw_snippets.txt]
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, security@halcyonhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP allowlist + ephemeral egress design for Private Endpoint POC

James — quick ops notes and the minimal firewall change set we recommend for a clean POC cutover.

Firewall change set (pasteable):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to destination IPs: any (we recommend FQDN allowlist to runtime.redwood-inference.com).
- Allow outbound TCP to reserved NAT addresses: x.x.x.8/29 (example) from the Redwood private endpoint subnets.
- Allow inbound from control-plane IPs: 203.0.113.21, 203.0.113.22, 203.0.113.23 only to management port 443 (for orchestration webhooks).
- Deny outbound to any non-443 ports from runtime instances by default; add exceptions only for approved vendor integrations.

Change window recommendation: schedule the firewall change and a single smoke test where we trigger a model inference and verify the egress IP seen from your side. I can run the smoke test remotely and provide tcpdump + TLS SNI evidence if needed.

Edge-case notes:
- Some appliances perform DNS over TLS to upstream resolvers; if present, allow resolver ips or FQDNs; wildcard FQDN allowlisting can help here.
- If you require per-request provenance headers for auditing, we can sign requests with a per-tenant header but that requires consent from your security team for PII handling.

I’ll be available on the infra call Monday to walk through the snippets.

Regards,
David Kim
Engineering Manager, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
